oewn-00529419-v.learner: to get back to the state you were in before after losing money.
examples: After the crash, it took the company's shares three years to recover.

oewn-02231615-v.learner: to take materials out of waste so that they can be used again.
examples: The plant recovers glass and metal from household rubbish.

oewn-01339223-v.learner: to put a new cover on something.
examples: She had the old armchair recovered in blue cloth.

oewn-07594444-n.learner: a small amount of food or drink that you eat or drink.
examples: Have a taste of the soup before you add more salt.
The summer job gave him his first taste of hard work.

oewn-05666071-n.learner: the ability to tell sweet, sour, bitter and salty things apart in your mouth.
examples: After her illness she lost her sense of taste for a month.

oewn-00884380-n.learner: a kind of sensing in which you tell things apart by using your taste buds.
examples: The cook named the hidden spice by taste alone.

oewn-03037971-n.learner: a board with electronic circuits printed on it that you push into a slot in a computer so the computer can do more.
examples: He fitted a new sound card to his computer.

oewn-14824204-n.learner: thin cardboard, usually cut in a rectangle.
examples: The children cut stars out of a sheet of gold card.

oewn-06645712-n.learner: a printed or written greeting that you leave behind to show that you came to visit.
examples: Finding no one at home, she left her card with the servant.

oewn-06806283-n.learner: a sign put up in a public place to advertise something.
examples: A card in the shop window advertised a room to let.

oewn-06519932-n.learner: a record of the scores in a game, as in golf.
examples: After the last hole, each player signed his card and handed it in.

oewn-10782010-n.learner: a funny, clever person who makes jokes.
examples: Uncle Joe is a real card and keeps everyone laughing at dinner.

connotation.why: fond, indulgent label for a person, set against plain 'joker' or 'wit'

oewn-06504930-n.learner: a list of the dishes you can order at a restaurant.
examples: Everything on the card looked good, so we asked the waiter to choose.

oewn-06497998-n.learner: in baseball, the list of batters in the order in which they will bat.
examples: The manager put his fastest runner first on the card.

oewn-07521110-n.learner: a lack of interest or feeling for others, shown by keeping yourself apart from them.
examples: After the quarrel there was a new distance in the way she spoke to him.

oewn-15197470-n.learner: a point that is far away in time.
examples: At this distance in time, few people remember why the war began.

oewn-15197259-n.learner: the amount of time between two moments.
examples: The distance between his two visits was barely a week.

oewn-00812219-v.learner: to not experience something, so that it does not happen to you.
examples: Our village escaped the storm that flooded the towns to the south.

oewn-02079296-v.learner: to run away quickly from a person or place.
examples: And upon Elizabeth's seeming really, with vexed and embarrassed looks, about to escape, she added, "Lizzy, I insist upon your staying and hearing Mr. Collins."

oewn-02605001-v.learner: to leave the place and life you are used to for a while, usually to enjoy yourself or have a change.
examples: Every August they escape to a small cottage by the sea.

oewn-00531097-v.learner: to come out or leak, as through a small hole.
examples: Gas was escaping from a crack in the pipe.

oewn-00364717-v.learner: to bring something to an end.
examples: The war interrupted his studies, and he never went back to them.

oewn-05945422-n.learner: a clear image in your mind that shows a lot about something.
examples: I still have a clear picture of the house where I grew up.

oewn-03931348-n.learner: an image of a person or scene made as a photo, whether printed, on a slide, or stored on a computer.
examples: She took a picture of the children on the beach.

oewn-06626039-n.learner: a film: a story told with sound and a run of images that seem to move.
examples: We went to see a picture at the cinema last night.

oewn-05774074-n.learner: a person or thing that is a typical example of some state or quality.
examples: After his holiday he looked the picture of health.

oewn-13960108-n.learner: a situation, thought of as something you can look at.
examples: The economic picture looks brighter than it did a year ago.

oewn-07012096-n.learner: drawings or other images used to decorate or explain a piece of writing.
examples: The pictures in this textbook explain each step of the experiment.

oewn-06288456-n.learner: the part of a television broadcast that you can see.
examples: The sound was fine, but the picture kept flickering.

oewn-07153623-n.learner: a discussion of a subject, as in a meeting.
examples: The committee's consideration of the budget took up the whole afternoon.

oewn-13344335-n.learner: money paid ahead of time so that someone will keep working for you when needed.
examples: In return for a yearly consideration paid in advance, the lawyer stayed ready to act for the firm.

oewn-07380889-n.learner: a way in which something departs from the usual standard or rule.
examples: Any difference from the approved design must be reported to the engineer.

oewn-13751346-n.learner: the number left when you take one number away from another; added to the number you took away, it gives the first number.
examples: The difference between 10 and 7 is 3.

oewn-02572443-v.learner: to act against a law, rule, contract or promise.
examples: Anyone who offends against these rules will be asked to leave.

connotation.why: frames rule-breaking as a wrong done, against plain 'break'
